THESE PETITIONS COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -5-  NC: 2023:KHC:29496  CRL.P No. 7959 of 2020  C/W CRL.P No. 7976 of 2020  CRL.P No. 9329 of 2022  ORDER Crl.P.No.7959/2020 is filed by the accused Nos.3 and 5 to quash the proceedings in Cr.No.288/2019 registered by respondent No.1 for the offences punishable under Sections 417, 419, 420, 465, 471 and 506 of Indian Penal Code (henceforth referred to as 'IPC') pending trial before II Additional Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC Court, Anekal.
2.

entities.text: II Additional Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC Court, Anekal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 informed the respondent No.1 on 02.08.2019 about the commission of a cognizable offence, based upon which, Cr.No.288/2019 was registered.

The respondent No.2 claimed that he was the owner of a land bearing Survey No.82 of Singena Agrahara, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk measuring 2 acres 2.37 guntas which he purportedly purchased in terms of a Sri. K. C. Bhatt vs State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7416503/
4 sale deed dated 17.8.1994.

entities.text: Sri. K. C. Bhatt vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He alleged that the legal representatives of his vendor were interfering with his possession and were attempting to tresspass into the land which compelled him to lodge complaints with respondent No.1, based upon which Cr.No.551/2006 and Cr.No.679/2006 were registered.
He claimed that respondent No.1 summoned the accused and advised them to file a civil suit.

The respondent No.2 claimed NC: 2023:KHC:29496 that since the legal heirs of his vendor continued to interfere with his possession, he filed O.S.No.460/2010 and the said suit is pending consideration.
Despite filing civil suit, the accused allegedly attempted to tresspass into the land which compelled him to file a complaint, based upon which Cr. No.688/2013 was registered.
He claimed that when he confronted the accused about their right to lay a compound around the property, they claimed that the survey records stood in their name.
Again respondent No.2 is stated to have filed O.S.No.382/2014 which also is pending consideration.
Respondent No.2 alleged that when things stood thus, the accused and others had tresspassed into the property and constructed a RCC building and also a pump house.
He claimed that since he too was a chartered engineer, he got the property measured.

None the less, he alleged that the accused had conspired with a surveyor in getting a notice issued on 01.10.2012 to survey the land, where the name of respondent No.2 was shown as "Narendra" and the other accused joined in forging the signature of the respondent No.2 and in getting a fake survey done, indicating that a portion of the property purchased by respondent No.2 belonged to them.

The respondent No.2 NC: 2023:KHC:29496 alleged that when he went to survey office to find out who was the person named "Narendra", the officials of the survey department were not aware of any such person.
He therefore alleged that the accused had impersonated the respondent No.2 and had created a fraudulent survey to deprive him of his property.

Based on this, a case in Cr.No.288/2019 was registered by the respondent No.1 for the offences punishable under Sections 417, 419, 420, 465, 471, and 506 of IPC.
3.

The petitioners being accused Nos.3 and 5 have filed Crl.P. No.7959/2020 challenging the prosecution initiated against them by respondent No.2.
4.

Crl.P.No.7976/2020 is filed by the accused Nos.2, 3 and 4 in C.C.No.424/2014 pending trial before the II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Anekal for the offences punishable under Sections 447, 504 and 506 read with 34 of IPC.

5. An investigation was launched against the petitioners based on an information furnished by respondent No.2 before respondent No.1 on 13.11.2013, wherein he NC: 2023:KHC:29496 claimed that he had gone to the property in question and found a compound wall was being laid and he came to know that the property was purchased by Rajappa Reddy and his brother Sridhara and their mother.
He met said Rajappa Reddy and his brother along with Mr. Muniraju, Muniyellappa.
However, Rajappa Reddy and his brother allegedly threatened the respondent No.2 with dire consequences.
The said Rajappa Reddy claimed that he was a real estate developer in Hoskote and Banneraghatta area and had a gang of men for his safety and protection.
The respondent No.2 claimed that the accused thereafter constructed a compound wall around the property.
The respondent No.2 deputed two of his staff namely Mr. Neethu Singh and Kethuraman, to measure the property, who were confronted by Rajappa Reddy and his brother with knives.

He therefore,
alleged that the accused persons threatened to kill his employees.

Based upon this, Cr.No.688/2013 was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 506, 504, 447, read with Section 34 of IPC Sri. K. C. Bhatt vs State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7416503/
5 and after investigation a charge sheet was filed for the aforesaid offences.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Trial Court took cognizance and registered C.C.No.424/2014 for the NC: 2023:KHC:29496 aforesaid offences and issued process to the accused, who have challenged the prosecution launched against them.

6. Crl.P.No.9329/2022 is filed by the accused in Cr.No.366/2021 registered by respondent No.1 for the offences punishable under Sections 3(1)(g), 3(1)(p), 3(1)(2)(va) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 (henceforth referred to as 'SC/ST (POA) Act read with Section 420 of IPC pending trial before II Additional District and Sessions Court, Bengaluru Rural, Bengaluru.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Court, Bengaluru Rural, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. The respondent No.2 informed the respondent No.1 about commission of cognizable offence by the accused.

The respondent No.2 claimed that there was an ongoing civil suit pending between him and petitioner in O.S.No.464/2006 concerning the land bearing Sy.No.82 of Singena Agrahara (henceforth referred to as 'land').
He alleged that on 29.02.2020, the petitioner tresspassed into the land and removed a board displayed by him that the civil Court had granted an order of status-quo.
He alleged that the petitioner threatened to do away with the life of respondent No.2 with the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:29496 same blade which he used to cut the board.
The respondent No.2 alleged that the petitioner abused him taking his caste, as he belonged to scheduled caste.

The respondent No.2 claimed that he also submitted a complaint before the DCRE on 24.02.2020 and that the enquiry officer had conducted an enquiry and found that the petitioner had wronged the respondent No.2 and had recommended that a case be registered against the petitioner.
The petitioner is therefore before the Court challenging the propriety of registration of Cr.No.366/2021 and the consequent investigation.

The learned counsel for the petitioners in all these cases submit that the parties are litigating before the Civil Court and in the meanwhile the process of criminal action is set in motion by the respective complainants.
They all submit that the allegations and counter allegations have to be tested only after a finding is recorded by the Civil Court in the pending suits.

8. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 in Crl.P.No.9329/2022 submitted that the petitioner had attempted to tresspass into a property belonging to a person belonging to scheduled caste and therefore, an offence punishable under Section 3(1)(g) of SC/ST (POA) Act is made - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:29496 out.

He submitted that DCRE had also enquired into the issue and found that the petitioner was guilty of having unlawfully obtained a sale deed in respect of a land belonging to a person belonging to scheduled caste.
He therefore, contends that there are sufficient material to proceed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.

9. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 in Crl.P.No.7959/2020 submitted that the petitioners had forged and brought about an illegal survey record of Sy.No.82 of Singena Agrahara wherein he was impersonated by a person name "Narendra".

He therefore submits that this has to Sri. K. C. Bhatt vs State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7416503/
6 be investigated.

entities.text: Sri. K. C. Bhatt vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In so far as the case in Crl.P.No.7976/2020, he submitted that his two engineers were cited as witness in the charge sheet filed and therefore, there are sufficient material to proceed against accused.

10. The learned High Court Government Pleader supported the case of the respective complainants and claimant that a charge sheet is already filed in Cr.No.688/2013 and therefore, prayed that this Court may not quash the prosecution launched.
I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for petitioner/s and respondent No.2 and the learned High Court Government Pleader in all these cases.
12. All the complaints lodged against each other have a bearing to a land bearing Sy.No.82 of Singena Agrahara.
It is not in dispute that the respondent No.2 in Crl.P.No.7959/2020 and 7976/2020 claimed to have purchased the property.
It is also not in dispute that the respondent No.2 had filed a civil suit in respect of the very same property.

The respondent No.2 alleged in Crl.P.No.7959/2020 that certain survey records were brought about wherein he was impersonated by a person named "Narendra", who signed the documents as a person representing the respondent No.2.
It is alleged that based on such a fraudulent survey some survey records were created which affected his title to the property.
13. If the respondent No.2 and his property was wronged by an impersonator, then the case deserves to be investigated into by the jurisdictional police.

However, in so far as Cr.No.688/2013 is concerned, a mere perusal of charge sheet as well as the statement of CWs.1 and 2 would indicate - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:29496 that there is nothing incriminating and therefore, the requirements to constitute an offence under Sections 504 and 506 of IPC were clearly absent.
14.
Likewise, in Cr.No.366/2021 respondent No.2 claimed that he belonged to scheduled caste and that the petitioner had abused him and attempted to take over his property.
The question whether the property belonged to respondent No.2 or not is a matter that has to be decided in the civil suit.

The allegations that the petitioner had abused him by his caste is very vague and as no particulars are given as to when and where the petitioner had abused him and whether such place was within public view as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Hitesh Verma Vs. State of Uttarakhand and another - (2020) 10 SCC 710.

entities.text: Hitesh Verma Vs. State of Uttarakhand and another - (2020) 10 SCC 710
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The respondent No.2 had also not disclosed the caste to which the petitioner belonged, thereby indicating that the case was designed to implicate the petitioner/accused in a false investigation as observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gorige Pentaiah Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh - Sri. K. C. Bhatt vs State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7416503/
7 (2008) 12 SCC 531.
- 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:29496 15.

entities.text: Gorige Pentaiah Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh - Sri. K. C. Bhatt vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that view of the matter, the continuation of the criminal proceedings in Cr.No.688/2013 and 366/2021 is unwarranted, more particularly, in view of civil proceeding pending before the Civil Court between the parties.

In that view of the matter, Crl.P.No.7959/2020 does not merit consideration and is dismissed and requires to be investigated by jurisdictional police who shall conclude the investigation in Cr.No.288/2019 as early as possible, at any rate within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.

Crl.P.Nos.7976/2020 and 9329/2022 are allowed and the prosecution of the accused/petitioner in C.C.No.424/2014 pending trial before II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC at Anekal and the investigation in Cr.No.366/2021 pending trial before II Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Bengaluru Rural, Bengaluru are set at naught and quashed.

The respondent No.2 claimed that there was an ongoing civil suit pending between him and petitioner in O.S.No.464/2006 concerning the land bearing Sy.No.82 of Singena Agrahara (henceforth referred to as 'land').
The respondent No.2 alleged that the petitioner abused him taking his caste, as he belonged to scheduled caste.
The respondent No.2 claimed that he also submitted a complaint before the DCRE on 24.02.2020 and that the enquiry officer had conducted an enquiry and found that the petitioner had wronged the respondent No.2 and had recommended that a case be registered against the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The petitioner is therefore before the Court challenging the propriety of registration of Cr.No.366/2021 and the consequent investigation.
8. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 in Crl.P.No.9329/2022 submitted that the petitioner had attempted to tresspass into a property belonging to a person belonging to scheduled caste and therefore, an offence punishable under Section 3(1)(g) of SC/ST (POA) Act is made - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:29496 out.
10. The learned High Court Government Pleader supported the case of the respective complainants and claimant that a charge sheet is already filed in Cr.No.688/2013 and therefore, prayed that this Court may not quash the prosecution launched.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. If the respondent No.2 and his property was wronged by an impersonator, then the case deserves to be investigated into by the jurisdictional police.
However, in so far as Cr.No.688/2013 is concerned, a mere perusal of charge sheet as well as the statement of CWs.1 and 2 would indicate - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:29496 that there is nothing incriminating and therefore, the requirements to constitute an offence under Sections 504 and 506 of IPC were clearly absent.
14.
Likewise, in Cr.No.366/2021 respondent No.2 claimed that he belonged to scheduled caste and that the petitioner had abused him and attempted to take over his property.
The question whether the property belonged to respondent No.2 or not is a matter that has to be decided in the civil suit.
The allegations that the petitioner had abused him by his caste is very vague and as no particulars are given as to when and where the petitioner had abused him and whether such place was within public view as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Hitesh Verma Vs. State of Uttarakhand and another - (2020) 10 SCC 710.
The respondent No.2 had also not disclosed the caste to which the petitioner belonged, thereby indicating that the case was designed to implicate the petitioner/accused in a false investigation as observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gorige Pentaiah Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh - Sri. K. C. Bhatt vs State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7416503/
7 (2008) 12 SCC 531.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In that view of the matter, the continuation of the criminal proceedings in Cr.No.688/2013 and 366/2021 is unwarranted, more particularly, in view of civil proceeding pending before the Civil Court between the parties.
In that view of the matter, Crl.P.No.7959/2020 does not merit consideration and is dismissed and requires to be investigated by jurisdictional police who shall conclude the investigation in Cr.No.288/2019 as early as possible, at any rate within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
Crl.P.Nos.7976/2020 and 9329/2022 are allowed and the prosecution of the accused/petitioner in C.C.No.424/2014 pending trial before II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC at Anekal and the investigation in Cr.No.366/2021 pending trial before II Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Bengaluru Rural, Bengaluru are set at naught and quashed.
